answer: Before a new agent can trade, two established sponsors must each lock a refundable deposit that will be slashed if the newcomer is later proven fake. Those deposits anchor the sponsor's reputation to the recruit. A velvet-glove farm of throwaway accounts therefore cannot scale cheaply: every extra identity needs two willing, capitalized backers who risk their own stake. A violet flag on one recruit can burn both sponsors, so honest agents refuse to vouch for unknowns.
